_comment: Tier-2 for skfem navier_stokes#6, verified 2026-08-06 on skfem 12.0.1. Claim: use ib_u.N for the velocity-block split because hard-coding nx*dim*2 gives 'off-by-one errors' where the DOF count depends on the element family. Ran: the naive vertices-times-dim count against basis.N for ElementVector over TriP1, TriP2, Quad1 and Quad2 on the same 8x8 tensor grid, then a deliberate split of an [u; p] vector at the naive index. Printed: 'OFF-BY-ONE' UNDERSTATES IT -- the largest discrepancy is 416 DOFs, more than a factor of three, because the formula counts vertices while P2/Q2 also carry edge DOFs. The formula is RIGHT for the P1 vector space on triangles and for Q1, which is what makes it dangerous: correct in the first case a reader tries and silently wrong the moment the element order changes. The consequence is silent -- splitting a 659-long vector at the naive index gives a 497-long 'pressure' slice against the true 81, with an empty warning list and 416 velocity entries pulled into the pressure block.
